findings.trigger: an overflow reachable only through a malformed length field is filed edge-case as 'rare input' and approved
findings.problem: Q3 treats rare input as unlikely, but attackers choose rare inputs, so exploitable defects leave the gate.
findings.fix: Rarity never lowers a trigger an untrusted party can choose; such a path is realistic.

findings.trigger: a new shell sink downstream of an agent that reads PR comments is classed speculative as 'an agent in the loop'
findings.problem: Q2 conflates actors who control the system with actors who can influence its inputs.
findings.fix: Out of model only an actor who already holds the access the attack would grant; influencers are in model; widening or newly relying on an untrusted feed counts.

findings.trigger: a reviewer or a realism check labels an exploitable HIGH edge-case and the loop reaches APPROVED
findings.problem: Moving a CRITICAL/HIGH out of the gate needs no human consent, unlike ACK.
findings.fix: Require a human decision for an edge-case or demoted CRITICAL/HIGH; show edge cases by severity.

findings.trigger: an open edge-case HIGH meets the commit gate or the docs/tech-pair loop that still gate on any open CRITICAL/HIGH

findings.trigger: the orchestrator dispatches the arbiter on its own and a HIGH leaves the verdict without a human decision
